consensus_summary: Primary meaning is sin, corruption, hypocrisy or false teaching that spreads pervasively (Passover removal, Jesus' warnings, Pauline usage); common alternative is positive kingdom growth in the leaven parable, with minority consistently-negative readings of that parable.
book_summary: Soured bread as the word made impure, embittered and puffed up; hidden corruption fermenting through the whole lump, purged before Passover and forbidden on the altar; NT identification as the Pharisees' corrupt doctrine.
book_core_identification: Hidden corruption (impure/embittered/puffed-up word) fermenting through the whole, specifically Pharisees' corrupt doctrine
boundary_disagreement: None material; book simply does not address the common positive kingdom-parable alternative recognized by consensus.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both identify leaven as the hidden, fermenting corruption (esp. false doctrine) that spreads through the lump and is purged at Passover/forbidden on the altar. Book's poetic descriptors and exclusive focus on the negative sense are wording or scope choices that do not alter the central referent or exclude cases belonging to the consensus primary meaning.
strongest_objection: Book's silence on the well-attested positive kingdom usage (Matt 13:33/Luke 13:20-21) could be read as an implicit claim of exclusive negativity.
